short: The first presidency, which defined what the office would and would not be.
full:
Washington took the oath on the balcony of Federal Hall in New York on 30 April 1789, seven weeks after the term formally began, because winter roads had delayed the counting of the electoral votes. He inherited a government that existed only on paper: no treasury, no courts, no precedent for anything a president did.

His two terms established the cabinet, the assumption of state debts pressed by Alexander Hamilton, a national bank, and a policy of neutrality between Britain and revolutionary France. He put down the Whiskey Rebellion in 1794 at the head of nearly 13,000 militia, demonstrating that federal taxes would be collected. His decision to stand down in 1797 rather than seek a third term set a two-term limit that held for 144 years until Franklin Roosevelt broke it. The Farewell Address, warning against permanent foreign alliances and the spirit of party, was read aloud in Congress for generations afterwards.
